statement: Subgroup performance with intervals is reported only for groups of at least 10 rows and, for a yes/no outcome, at least 5 rows of each class; smaller groups are named but not scored; an amount column is grouped into thirds at its 1/3 and 2/3 quantiles and a code column by its levels.
decision: Which subgroups are scored and how a column is grouped
user_sees: "Too few rows of one class to score this group (fewer than 5)." / "Fewer than 10 rows: not scored."
notes: [part id F2-025] test_explore_4_decision_curve.py::test_4_a_group_with_too_few_events_is_named_not_scored pins the rule. With 5 events DeLong/influence intervals have poor coverage; the floors are unsourced conventions. MIN_GROUP_ROWS/EVENTS :53-54.

statement: On the pre-fit shelf, ridge scores 2.0 from 2,000 training rows, 1.0 below 2,000 (under least squares' and the screened elastic net's 1.5), 3.0 when predictors are at least as many as rows (below the elastic net's 4.0), is fair at most 2.0 under inference, and below 50 rows carries the concern that inner CV picks the penalty from very few rows.
user_sees: Concerns: "{p} predictors for {n} rows: it keeps every one, each shrunk." / "With {n} rows the inner cross-validation picks the penalty from very few rows."
claimed_basis: RECIPES §2.6 conventions; the below-2,000 value is chosen "so the two families the reference journeys pick today stay first" (ridge.py:25-28).
notes: [part id F4-017] CODE-VS-DOC: RECIPES §2.6 lists only 2.0 and 3.0 at p ≥ n; the 1.0 below 2,000 rows (SMALL_SCORE, ridge.py:72) is added in code to protect the journeys' picks, not for a methods reason. test_ridge_family.py::test_the_shelf_scores_are_recipes_conventions and ::test_ridge_never_displaces_the_first_two_families_the_journeys_pick pin it. FEW_ROWS 50 at :73.

statement: Under Estimate or Describe, a Belsley condition index of 30 or more with at least two model-matrix columns having variance-decomposition proportion 0.5 or more marks a near dependency among the exposure and adjustment set; when the exposure's proportions summed over those near dependencies reach 0.5, which of the dependent columns are held fixed changes what the exposure's estimate means (more exposure at fixed partners means less of what it replaces), so it is a Decide at the adjustment question and graded 'act on it'.
regime: Estimate or Describe; outcome-blind; model matrix built as the fit builds it (intercept and columns scaled to unit length, not centered); any lens
decision: Whether the collinear-predictors noticing is a Decide routed to the adjustment-set question (band 2, changes the question)
user_sees: "`sugar` is close to a fixed mix of {others}: holding them fixed, more `sugar` means less of what it replaces, so which of them stay in the model changes what the estimate means. It is decided at the adjustment-set question."
claimed_basis: Belsley, Kuh & Welsch (1980, §3.3) for the 30 and 0.5 thresholds (code comment)
notes: [part id F6-003] Code at materiality.py:773-776 (thresholds), 808-822 (belsley), 883-904 (decision). SURFACING_POLICY §2.5 row K5 instead says |r| >= 0.9 pairs with default band 1; code uses Belsley and bands 0/2. Summing an exposure's proportions across several near dependencies and comparing to 0.5 is the app's own heuristic, not BKW's. The substitution reading ('means less of what it replaces') is exact for parts summing to a total but is stated for any near dependency. Tests in test_collinear_adjustment.py exercise fixtures, not the thresholds' validity.

statement: A bootstrap band whose failed refits are dropped is conditioned on the resamples a model could be fit on; with at least 90% of refits succeeding this barely moves it, but with more failures it describes another population of resamples, so no band is drawn below 90% success.
regime: substitution band with failing refits (e.g. a resample missing a class)
user_sees: 171 of 200 refits succeeded; a band needs at least 90% of them
claimed_basis: 'A practitioner convention, not a sourced threshold'
notes: Code substitution.py:637-648. test_wp5::test_3_a_band_needs_a_stated_minimum_share_of_successful_refits checks the refusal only.

statement: When the study-design question is unanswered, analyzing the table as an observational study (people observed as they were, not randomized, not sampled by the outcome, not matched) is a safe default under every goal, provided it is stated and listed for confirmation.
regime: any table whose design slot (q:study-design) is unanswered
decision: the study-design slot; which analysis lane runs
user_sees: Read as an observational study: people were observed as they were, not assigned or sampled by their outcome. Change it if they were randomized, sampled by the outcome or matched.
claimed_basis: crosswalk disagreement 10 (the design slot); V2X_SEAMS seam guard 6 and recommendation 6
notes: Also designs.py:151-153 (design_of), interview.py:449-454, surfacing.py:382 (default:design_observational). For an undeclared case-control sample the observational lane can report prevalence/risk-scale measures that case_control.py refuses under every goal (S4-061); the case-control detection signals (S4-072, S4-073) are noticings only and do not route.

statement: Change-in-estimate selection among covariates already judged pre-exposure causes cannot detect mediators or colliders, and for an odds ratio or hazard ratio with a common outcome the estimate changes from non-collapsibility even without confounding, so it is block-and-record under inference and conflicts with OR/HR estimands for common outcomes.
regime: inference; data-driven adjustment by change-in-estimate; OR or HR with a common outcome for the invalidity part
user_sees: Block-and-record label stating it cannot see mediators or colliders and is invalid for an OR or HR with a common outcome
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 1(c); §2 'an OR or HR with a common outcome conflicts with change-in-estimate'
notes: Doc-level; check estimand.py (slice S6) for an implementation. No implementation found: grep for change-in-estimate over turbotab/ (non-test code) returns nothing, so this ruling is doc-only at present.

statement: Under prediction with the surveyed-population answer, cross-validated performance estimates population performance only if the folds keep whole PSUs within strata and every loss, calibration and comparison is survey-weighted (design-based cross-validation), while under the sample answer unweighted scores describe the procedure's performance on these rows only.
decision: Fold construction and weighting of prediction scores
user_sees: "Design-based cross-validation over {p} PSUs in {s} strata, every score weighted by `{w}`; {df} design degrees of freedom." / "Unweighted: the scores are the procedure's performance on these {n} ro...
claimed_basis: Wieczorek, Guerin & McMahon 2022, Stat 11:e454 (design-based K-fold CV); MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 13.
notes: Fit code in turbotab/core/models/design_cv.py (outside area C). | Inventory source id: F1-043.

statement: Under the fit and its imputation model a predictor with exactly two values needs no code-or-amount answer, because coding it as one indicator or as a numeric amount gives the same slope, interval and every prediction (only the intercept's reference changes), and both imputation models fill it as a yes/no; when a unit's rows are combined the two readings differ (mean = a share vs the most frequent value), so there it is asked.
decision: Whether the fit waits for a two-valued predictor's coding answer.
user_sees: No question is asked for a two-valued predictor at the fit.
claimed_basis: Docstring reasoning only (readings.py:1600-1608); methods.imputation.column_kind (imputation.py:127) imputes any two-valued numeric column as binary.
notes: Holds for linear/GLM models with an intercept and for trees. Two values other than 0/1 (e.g., 1 and 5) change the slope's scale (per-unit vs per-level) though not predictions; with penalized models whose penalty is not scale-invariant, or with splines/interactions on the column, the two codings can differ. The 'same interval' wording refers to the reparameterized coefficient. | Inventory source id: F3-019.

statement: In a nutrition exposure-outcome analysis, demographic covariates (age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, income/poverty ratio, occupation, marital status) are pre-exposure common causes of the exposure and the outcome and belong in the adjustment set as confounders (the criterion's answers: causes exposure yes, causes outcome yes, after exposure no).
regime: Inference (total effect) with a declared exposure; covariates named as demographics; any study design, including cross-sectional.
decision: Pre-filled answers on the adjustment card (modified disjunctive cause criterion), confirmed in one tap per block.
user_sees: Demographics: "set before the diet was measured, and the field's Models 1 and 2 adjust for them as what else could explain the link"
claimed_basis: NUTRITION_PACK §08 (Models 1 and 2); VanderWeele 2019 Eur J Epidemiol 34:211-219.
notes: Answers PRE_EXPOSURE covariate_guesses.py:81; derived role via estimand.py:694 derive; blocks estimand.py:927 guess_blocks. turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_leash.py::test_1_the_guess_follows_the_exposure_outcome_pairing pins the guesses to the spec (not a test of the claim). | Inventory source id: F3-040.

statement: When missingness of the predictors differs by sociodemographic group, the sound missing-data handling for inference is multiple imputation with the group in the imputation model, while complete-case analysis must state its assumption.
decision: Quality-by-group lever routes to the missing-values question with this option Recommended.
user_sees: "The missing-values question, with these differences in view" — "Multiple imputation with the group in its model when missingness differs by group; complete cases states its assumption".
notes: This lever only routes to the missing-values question (methods.missing ranks the options there; outside area C). The claim does not condition on the group being related to the outcome or the missingness mechanism. | Inventory source id: F6-015.

statement: Each cross-validated score's standard error, and the interval for each pair of families' difference (the corrected repeated k-fold t over at least 10 × K folds), computed on the user's rows, tell whether two models differ, in place of a rule about sample size.
user_sees: Each cross-validated score carries its standard error, and each pair of families an interval for their difference, computed on these rows. Read whether two models differ from that interval
notes: test_ms6_prediction_validation.py::test_2_the_corrected_repeated_kfold_t_matches_a_numpy_hand_computation checks the arithmetic only. No unbiased estimator of CV variance exists (Bengio & Grandvalet 2004); the corrected t is a heuristic with approximate coverage. BEATS_PREDICT ruling 4 says 'not distinguishable' is never read from an interval crossing zero alone, in tension with 'read whether two models differ from that interval'.

statement: Under-reporting of energy is systematic and concentrated among people with higher BMI and weight-conscious participants, so excluding under-reporters when the outcome is adiposity removes a non-random slice of the studied population, which is why many analyses keep everyone.
regime: dietary lens; intake screens; adiposity-related outcomes
decision: the exclusions card's why, term and drawer
user_sees: Under-reporting is concentrated in people with higher BMI, so excluding under-reporters when the outcome is adiposity removes a non-random slice of exactly the population studied.
notes: Also content.py:819-822 and term 850-851; coach.py:271-282 compares the excluded and kept rows' median BMI.

statement: Under Predict, each continuous predictor of least squares, ridge and the elastic net enters as a restricted cubic spline (Harrell's knots, placed in each training fold) by default when Riley's sample-size criteria hold for the terms it makes (here 3,916 rows needed for 73 terms at an expected shrinkage of at least 0.9).
user_sees: the 73 terms this makes; 3,916 would be enough.
notes: The capture adopted it after a cross-validated benchmark (stated). Riley's criteria count parameters, while ridge and the elastic net change the effective degrees of freedom.
